The correct answer is __**Kathak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rani Karnaa borne in 1939 in **Hyderabad, Sindh** (now in Pakistan).
 
• Rani Karnaa was a distinguished Indian classical dancer known for her expertise in Kathak.
 
• She trained under legendary **gurus such as Nrityacharya Narayan Prasad, Pandit Sunder Prasad, and Pandit Birju Maharaj.**
 
• Rani Karnaa was renowned for blending the **Jaipur and Lucknow gharanas**, creating a unique and aesthetically rich style.
 
• She received numerous accolades, including the **Padma Shri in 2014** and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996.

**Kathak:**

 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of** Indian classical dance**, originating from the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The dance form evolved during the **Bhakti movement**, incorporating stories of Hindu gods, particularly Krishna.
 
• It further developed under the patronage of **Mughal emperors, integrating Persian elements.**
 
• Kathak has **three main gharanas (schools)** - **Jaipur, Lucknow, and Banaras**.
 
• The Jaipur gharana emphasizes intricate footwork, while the Lucknow gharana focuses on facial expressions and graceful hand movements.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the chairman of the National Commission for Backward classes in December 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Hansraj Gangaram Ahir**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hansraj Gangaram Ahir was appointed as the chairman of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) in December 2022.
 
• He is a **former Union Minister of State for Home Affairs.**
 
• Ahir has been a prominent leader from Maharashtra and has served as a Member of Parliament.

**National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)**

 
• **102nd Constitution Amendment Act, 2018** granted constitutional status to the NCBC.
 
• **Article 338B** provides the NCBC with the authority to investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the socially and educationally backward classes under the Constitution or under any other law.
 
• **Constitution (127th Amendment) bill, 2021:** This amendment allows states and union territories to prepare and maintain their own lists of SEBCs.
 
• **Article 342A:** Initially, this article empowered only the President to specify SEBCs in consultation with the Governor of the concerned state. The 2021 amendment restored the states’ authority in this matter.
 
• **Mandal Commission** established in 1979, it recommended reservations for OBCs in government jobs and educational institutions, leading to the implementation of** 27% reservation** for OBCs in 1990.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** **Development Process of NCBC**

 
• The** first backward classes commission** was established under the chairmanship of **Kaka Kalelkar** to identify the socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• The commission submitted its report in 1955, but its recommendations were not implemented.
 
• Second Backward Classes Commission (1979) (Mandal Commission):Headed by **B.P. Mandal,** this commission was tasked with identifying the **criteria for defining** socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• The Mandal Commission’s report, submitted in 1980,** recommended a 27% reservation** for OBCs in government jobs and educational institutions. These recommendations were implemented in 1990.
 
• The Supreme Court, in the landmark **Indra Sawhney & Others v. Union of India case**, directed the establishment of a permanent body to examine and recommend the inclusion and exclusion of various Backward Classes. This led to the creation of the NCBC.
 
• The NCBC was constituted as a **statutory body under National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 **to address the issues of backward classes.

**Structure of NCBC**

 
• **Chairperson:** Appointed by the President
 
• Vice-Chairperson
 
• **Three Other Members: **These members are appointed by the President and include individuals with special knowledge or experience in matters related to backward classes.

questions.question: With which sport is the Burdwan Trophy associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weightlifting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Weightlifting:

__
 
• Weightlifting is a sport in which athletes compete in lifting a barbell loaded with weight plates from the ground to overhead.
 
• Athletes compete in two specific ways of lifting the barbell overhead.
 
• These are:
 
 
• the snatch
 
• the clean and jerk.
 
 

Explanation:__

__
 
• The snatch is a wide-grip lift, in which the weighted barbell is lifted overhead in one motion.
 
• The clean and jerk is a combination lift, in which the weight is first taken from the ground to the front of the shoulders (the clean), and then from the shoulders to overhead (the jerk).
 
• The clean and press, wherein a clean was followed by an overhead press, was formerly also a competition lift but was discontinued due to difficulties in judging proper form.
 
• To keep competing the player has to increase at least 5 kg of weight between two attempts if the first one is successful.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Few rules(officiating):

 
• During the competition, the snatch event takes place first, followed by a short intermission, and then the clean and jerk event.

options.text: Fluid mosaic model of a cell

__
 
• **G.N. Ramachandran** is renowned for his significant contributions to biochemistry, particularly for elucidating the triple helical structure of collagen.
 
• His work established that collagen, a key structural protein in connective tissues, consists of** three polypeptide chain**s that form a right-handed triple helix.
 
• The discovery of collagen's structure has** implications for medicine**, particularly in understanding diseases related to connective tissues.
 
• Ramachandran's work has earned him recognition as a **pioneer in structural biology,** influencing subsequent research in the field.

• **Fluid Mosaic Model of a Cell:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Singer and Nicolson in 1972**, this model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic and flexible structure with a mosaic of various proteins floating in or on the fluid lipid bilayer.
 
• It highlights the importance of membrane proteins in functions such as signaling, transport, and maintaining cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is the** outer boundary of the cell **that separates its interior from the external environment.
 
• Composed of a lipid bilayer with embedded proteins, it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, playing a crucial role in cell communication and homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Bodies:**

questions.question: The Vienna Convention is related to ____________.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Vienna Convention**, formally known as the Vienna Convention for the** Protection of the Ozone Layer**, was adopted in **1985** to address the depletion of the ozone layer.
 
• The convention is a **legally binding agreement** that aims to promote international cooperation to protect the ozone layer. It encourages countries to: 
 
 
• Exchange information and conduct research on the ozone layer 
 
• Adopt laws and regulations to protect the ozone layer 
 
• Develop controls for ozone layer development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montreal Protocol:**

 
 
• Adopted in** 1987**, this protocol aims to **phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances,** such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
 
• It is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties, leading to significant recovery of the ozone layer.
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol:**
 
 
• Adopted in **1997**, this international agreement commits its parties to **reduce greenhouse gas emissions**, based on the premise that global warming exists and human-made CO2 emissions have caused it.
 
• The protocol emphasizes binding commitments for developed countries to mitigate climate change.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• Adopted in **2015,** this landmark accord aims to** limit global warming** to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
 
• It encourages countries to set their emission reduction targets and report on their progress.
 
 
 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**
 
 
• Established in** 1992**, this convention aims to conserve biological diversity, promote sustainable use of its components, and ensure fair sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of preserving ecosystems and species.
 
 
 
• **UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):**
 
 
• Adopted in **1992**, this treaty sets the framework for international efforts to combat climate change, with periodic Conferences of the Parties (COP) to assess progress and set binding commitments.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and select the correct option.

A. Directive Principles of State Policy consists of all the ideals which the state should follow and keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws for the country.

B. It can be enforced by the Judiciary.

C. They can be suspended during a national emergency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Directive Principles of State Policy

 
• Articles 36-51 under Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deal with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• They are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
 
• It refers to the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws. e.g. the Government should try to ensure equal pay for equal work for men and women etc. 
 
• Non-justiciable nature on recommendations of Tej Bahadur committee Report
 
• Positive Connotation – Establishes social and economic democracy.
 
• Promote the concept of a Welfare State and Inclusive Growth.
 
• Precursors of Panchayat Raj Institution (Art. 40- Village Panchayat)
 
• Fundamental in governance and apply in policy makings – Art. 37
 
• Novel features and Soul of the constitution – B.R Ambedkar
 
• DPSP is the Conscience of the constitution – Granville Austin
 
• Constitutional instructions to – Legislature, executive, and administration of the state.
 
• Enabling in nature – Enables government for a comprehensive program of social and economic justice, unlike FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS.
 
• Non-justiciable, Non-self-executory, non-enforceable by a court of law.
 
• Government can implement provisions of DPSP by legislative actions.

Significance of DPSP

 
• Helps courts as Guiding Light in determining and examining the constitutional validity of acts/rules/regulations.
 
• Symbolizes the idea of a welfare state and amplifies social and economic justice as entailed in the Preamble.
 
• They impose a moral obligation on the state authorities for their application, however, public opinion is the real force behind them.
 
• Serves as moral precepts for – Legislature, executive, and administration of state
 
• They serve as a Common Minimum Programme for every government irrespective of their manifestos and political ideologies.
 
• The Directives are the life-giving provisions of the Constitution. They constitute the stuff of the Constitution and its philosophy of social justice. – L. M Singhvi. Hence, Option 1 is correct.
 
• Directives lay down that the goal of Indian polity is ‘economic democracy’ as distinguished from ‘political democracy’ (Fundamental rights) – R. Ambedkar
 
• Supplements and complements Fundamental Rights (Part III).
 
• Serves as benchmarks and yardstick for people to gauge the performance of govt.
 
• DPSPs are intended to be a guide, friends, and philosophers of the ruling party in legislative and executive acts.
 
• Serves as an important tool for opposition parties to ensure accountability of the executive and exercise influence and control over the government.

__
 
• The **non-cooperation movement** was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 to resist British rule in India through non-violent means.

• The **distribution of spinning wheels** was encouraged to promote self-reliance and the use of khadi (hand-spun cloth).

• It was characterized by the use of non-violent methods such as non-payment of taxes, surrender of titles, and boycott of British educational institutions and law courts.
 
• The movement was eventually called off by Gandhi in 1922 following the Chauri Chaura incident, where a violent clash led to the death of police officers.
 
• The **Lahore Session** in 1929 was a turning point as it marked the formal adoption of the goal of Poorna Swaraj or complete independence from British rule.

The average weight of Rohan and his three friends is 62 kg.

Rohan's weight is 8 kg more than the average weight of his three friends.

**Formula used:**

Let the average weight of Rohan's three friends be x kg.

Rohan's weight = x + 8

Total weight of Rohan and his three friends = 4 × 62

**Calculation:**

Total weight of Rohan and his three friends = 4 × 62

⇒ 248 kg

Weight of Rohan = x + 8

⇒ 4x + 8 = 248

⇒ 4x = 240

⇒ x = 60

Rohan's weight = x + 8

⇒ 60 + 8 = 68 kg

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

Strength at the start of 2021 = S × 1.20 × 0.80 × 1.20

⇒ S × (1.20)² × 0.80

⇒ S × 1.44 × 0.80

⇒ S × 1.152

⇒ Increase by 15.2%
